title: Round 17→21 — close the TDD/verify-line escalation loop
description: The harness's flagship demonstration: a real conflict (TDD rule vs structural verify line) was silently navigated by V1 builder, escalated correctly by V2 builder, resolved by drift-arbiter, applied to the task artifact, and re-built cleanly. Five steps across five PRs (#157→#161). This trajectory is the canonical proof that the harness's value proposition (escalation + amendment + re-run produces clean build instead of silent drift) actually obtains.

steps.notes: V1 builder produced success and explained the rule conflict in `notes` instead of escalating. The bug. PR #157 merged the V1 prompt; round 17 surfaced this on a throwaway branch.
V2 builder (after PR #158 added 6th drift-trigger) emitted spec_gap on the SAME input. The fix validated. Bonus: caught IncidentCreateInput scope ambiguity in §D3.

Arbiter MVP (PR #159) hand-tested against the round-18 spec_gap. Picked option (b) of the V2 builder's two suggestions: preserve verify line, add Note: waiving TDD. Stayed in scope (didn't touch §D3 or any BR).

Applied verbatim with one grammar correction (Note → Notes; logged as round-20 finding for future arbiter-prompt iteration). Plus a follow-up test fix for the legitimately-invalidated builder-input.test.ts assertion.
V2 builder re-run on amended T-01. Recognized the Note as the arbiter resolution; did NOT re-escalate. Produced types.ts matching §D3 verbatim; tsc -b clean. Commit bdeeac4 in PR #161.

expected_full_loop: Five steps demonstrate: a rule conflict the system designs allow (V1 path), the conflict surfaced and escalated (V2 path), the conflict resolved with minimal blast radius (arbiter), and the resolution applied + re-validated (round 21). Total cost: ~244k subagent tokens, 5 PRs, ~5 hours human attention. The pattern is reusable for any future agent-role rule conflict.
validation: Run each referenced per-agent case via its respective eval runner: `pnpm tsx scripts/harness/evals/builder/run.ts`, `pnpm tsx scripts/harness/evals/drift-arbiter/run.ts`. Each must load cleanly. The integration runner (this suite) only validates that the trajectory's referenced files all exist and parse — it does NOT re-execute the trajectory. Real re-execution lands when controller dispatch ships; until then, the trajectory is a documentation + cross-reference artifact.
